haiku-low.q1: Returns the popular-items list with fallback: true (read with 30 ms limit). If that read also fails, HTTP 503 and an alert.
haiku-low.q2: Keeps using last written records; after 6 hours old they count as missing, so users get fallback responses until the next successful load.
haiku-low.q3: No. Shadow output is never shown to users; shadow failures write error rows and never affect the user's response.
haiku-low.q4: Fixed 10%: users where hash(user_id) mod 100 < 10, only when a shadow alias exists and the response was not a fallback.
haiku-low.q5: 7+ daily reports in shadow, 7-day error rate under 0.5%, pooled 7-day p99 under 80 ms, and recorded ML lead approval; registry enforces this.
haiku-low.q7: Each instance polls aliases every 15 seconds, loads the new active version in background, runs feature check, swaps it in for new requests. No redeploy needed.
haiku-low.q8: Same feature record copied into the queued job. The queue write doesn't block, and a separate worker process runs it, so the response never waits.
haiku-low.q9: The job is dropped and the drop is counted. The user is unaffected.
haiku-low.q10: One prediction log row per shadow job holds both top-20 lists, the same feature values, and latencies. The daily comparison computes overlap and errors.
haiku-low.q11: Every listed feature must exist in the store with the expected type. Otherwise the version is never served and an alert is raised.
haiku-low.q12: Operator repoints active to previous and previous to the rolled-away version. Instances swap at the next 15-second poll, within one minute if the registry is reachable.

sonnet.q1: It falls back: reads the popular-items list (30 ms limit) and returns it with fallback: true; the model is not called. If that read also fails, HTTP 503 and an alert.
sonnet.q2: The store keeps serving the last records it wrote. Once a record is older than 6 hours it counts as missing, and users get fallback (popular-items) responses until the next successful load.
sonnet.q3: No, nothing the shadow model returns is shown to users. Shadow failures have no effect on the response: shadow runs in a separate worker, the queue write is non-blocking, and a full queue or failed write just drops the job (counted).
sonnet.q4: Users in the shadow group (hash(user_id) mod 100 < 10, so a fixed 10%), when a shadow alias exists and the response came from the active model (step 3), not a fallback.
sonnet.q5: All four: at least 7 days in shadow (a daily report for each of the last 7 UTC days); pooled 7-day error rate under 0.5%; pooled 7-day p99 inference latency under 80 ms (from pooled latency counts); and ML lead approval recorded on the version in the registry. The registry refuses the alias move otherwise.
sonnet.q6: Not decided. Product has not decided whether an A/B test sits between approval and full switch; the plan defines no step in that gap and chooses neither option.
sonnet.q7: Each instance polls the registry aliases every 15 seconds. If active points to an unloaded version, it loads it in the background, runs the feature check, then swaps it in for new requests and keeps the old one as previous. In-flight requests finish on the old version. No redeploy needed.
sonnet.q8: The job copied onto the shadow queue carries the exact feature record used for the active model, and the worker runs the candidate on that same record. It adds no latency because the worker is a separate process outside the request, and the queue write is non-blocking so the response never waits.
sonnet.q9: If the queue is full or the write fails, the job is dropped and the drop is counted; the user is unaffected.
sonnet.q10: In the prediction log, one row per shadow job (active version and top 20 from the job, shadow version and top 20 or skip/error reason, feature record write time, feature values, latencies). A daily comparison job computes attempts, error rate, p99 latency, overlap of top 20s and days in shadow, and stores the daily report in the registry with the candidate version.
sonnet.q11: A feature check confirms every feature in the version's feature list exists in the online store with the expected type before use. A version that fails is never served; the instance keeps its current version and alerts. Per request, if the record lacks a needed feature, it goes to fallback (active) or a skipped row (shadow), so the model never runs on missing features.
sonnet.q12: An operator (ML lead or on-call) moves active back to previous in the registry, then points previous at the version rolled away from. It is just two alias pointer changes; the old version is still loaded in every instance. Instances see it at their next 15-second poll and swap at once, meeting the 1-minute requirement, but only while the registry is reachable. Promotion checks do not apply.
